A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same compositional ReLU-network study. Their complete main texts, six figures, two tables, and Appendices A.1–A.3 are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original function-approximation experiments, including minimum and mean MSE over 30 models per configuration in Tables 1–2 and neuron-output analyses in Figures 5–6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and results in Section 4, Tables 1–2, and Figures 5–6.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same four-neuron compositional architecture, trainable triangle peaks, differentiability-constrained scaling, and subsequent training of the underlying weights. The reparameterization terminology and expanded network diagram do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic one-dimensional targets: x³, x¹¹, tanh(3x), and a quarter-period sine curve. No additional datasets, domains, or evaluation scenarios appear.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same Kaiming/default and RAAI comparators and the same pretraining and differentiability variants. v1's 'No Optimization' is renamed 'No Pretraining'; its experimental role and scores are unchanged.

E3.justification: Both specify 500 evenly spaced points on [0,1], four neurons per hidden layer, five hidden layers, Adam for 1000 epochs, and MSE. v2's explicit statement that no train–test split is used clarifies the existing interpolation experiment rather than reporting a protocol change.

E4.justification: The comparisons with versus without pretraining and differentiability constraints are retained, along with the neuron-output case studies in Figures 5–6. No new ablation, robustness test, or supplementary empirical analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Both report minimum and mean losses for 30 models per configuration, without confidence intervals or significance tests. Adding 'n = 30' to v2's table captions repeats information already provided in v1 Section 4.1.

E6.justification: All 40 MSE values in Tables 1–2 are identical. However, v2 Section 4.4 drops v1's specific observation of structural retention to approximately six or seven layers, retaining only 'greater depths'. Section 4.2 also corrects RAAI's 'low mean' wording to 'high mean error', consistent with the unchanged tables.

T1.justification: The main recurrence and appendix results are retained; v1 Lemma 3.3 becomes v2 Lemma A.2. v2 formalizes the continuity reduction as Lemma 3.1. Its rewritten Lemma 3.2 proof also introduces a local error: s_{i+1} appears in W'_{i+1}, whereas v1 correctly applies that factor to the weighted summand.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains reparameterized pretraining that preserves exponentially many activation regions, followed by weight refinement, yielding substantially lower approximation errors on simple one-dimensional functions. The rewritten abstract and new conclusion retain this contribution and its scope.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds substantive discussion of dense region boundaries and repeated copies of the input interval as potentially useful properties for extensions. It also explicitly discusses polynomial representation by assembled networks. The convexity and twice-differentiability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly discloses the absence of a train–test split for the noiseless synthetic experiments and identifies Figure 6's examples as top-performing models. These provide additional documentation of existing experiments without establishing changed settings or reruns.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Chmielewski-Anders (2020), Gibou et al. (2019), Nag et al. (2023), and Qi et al. (2024). The existing positioning relative to triangle-wave approximation constructions and initialization methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the explanatory prose are rewritten. Mathematical definitions precede the architecture explanation, a lemma moves to the appendix, terminology shifts from manifolds to reparameterization, and concluding remarks and broader-impact sections are added.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 2 gains a full multilayer-network panel, Figure 4 is redrawn with colored, rearranged panels, and figures and tables receive revised captions and placement. These substantially change presentation while retaining the empirical displays.

improvement.justification: The reorganized explanation and expanded Figures 2 and 4 make the construction easier to follow, while Section 4.1 clarifies that evaluation concerns interpolation without held-out testing. These provide a limited net improvement in clarity and transparency, tempered by the new coefficient error in Lemma 3.2. The numerical evidence and main theoretical conclusions remain unchanged.
